humanities_role_explanation: Culturally specific questions (history, religion, customs, language and literature, food) supply the items, but the competence measured is general multilingual long-form QA quality (surface, factuality, relevance), not disciplinary humanities competence.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only questions in 23 languages with long-form text answers; reference answers exist for a subset.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Long-form QA on culturally specific questions ('culturally specific long-form question answering'). Answers are evaluated for factuality (claim verification via VeriScore), relevance (LLM-as-judge), and surface issues (wrong language, repetition); human raters score and rank answers.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to one task (long-form QA on culturally specific questions) and framework.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Claude-3-Opus, Gemini-1.5-Pro, GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-4o, Aya-Expanse-32B, Llama-3-70B, Mixtral-8x22B.

quantitative_metrics.note: Wrong-language %, repetition %, factual precision (VeriScore), relevance %, combined overall score S, human 5-point ratings and rankings with CLMM.

summary: CaLMQA is a translation-free dataset of 51.7K culturally specific long-form questions across 23 languages, collected from community forums and from hired native speakers for low-resource languages. Seven LLMs are evaluated with automatic surface, factuality and relevance metrics plus native-speaker human evaluation in five languages. Culturally specific questions yield less factual answers than culturally agnostic ones, and low-resource languages show severe surface errors.
key_findings: Factual precision is 64-71% for culturally agnostic vs 45-52% for culturally specific answers. Open-weight models perform much worse on low-resource languages (LLaMA-3-70B wrong language 76.0/70.0%). Human raters prefer GPT-4-Turbo, then Claude-3-Opus, then Mixtral. Culturally agnostic answers have a 67% chance of a higher rating. Omissions and factuality issues predict ratings.
facets_explanation: Questions were collected by Prolific crowdworkers from community forums (923 with real user answers), scaled by GPT-4o-mini filtering (50,227 additional), and written by Upwork native speakers for low-resource languages (548). Model answers are scored by VeriScore factuality against Google search evidence, an LLM relevance judge, and native-speaker human ratings; no single gold answer is matched. Culture-specific questions are defined as having answers dependent on cultural or regional context, with per-language native questions.
results_explanation: Table 2 reports overall score S of 'GPT-4O 56.9 / 49.2' (agnostic / specific) and 'GPT-4-TURBO 56.9 / 48.7'; the headline 56.9 is the combined S on the culturally agnostic portion. The gap points of 18 are derived from factual precision 69.6 vs 52.2 (GPT-4o), comparing culturally agnostic vs culturally specific questions (treated as a difficulty-type comparison). No human baseline is reported; human evaluation compares models only. The evaluation set is 3,644 questions.

humanities_role.quote: we collect that cultural knowledge in CALMQA

dataset_size.quote: CALMQA – the first textual multilingual long-form question answering (LFQA) dataset, with 51.7K questions across 23 languages

evaluation_set_size.quote: we assemble an evaluation set of 3,644 questions from three sources

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: Each model is prompted with a question from our dataset in a zero-shot setup without instructions.

gold_source.quote: we hire 29 native speakers (1-3 annotators per language, depending on their availability) on Upwork

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: verifies automatically extracted claims against retrieved evidence

gold_community_dependent.quote: have different answers depending on the cultural or regional context

answer_multiplicity.quote: rate it on a 5-point scale (excellent, good, average, poor, unusable)

reported_format_gap_kind.quote: Generated answers to culturally agnostic questions tend to be more factual (64%– 71%) than answers to culturally specific questions (45%–52%).

reported_cultural_asymmetry.quote: The closed models significantly outperform the open models on the low-resource languages, scoring mostly 22 – 66 while the open models mostly score below 10.
